conventions.convention: The fixed height is h(x)=x₄ on the oriented unit S³ in R⁴. Bridge number minimizes the number of maxima over ambient-isotopic Morse representatives.
A crossing change switches only the overpassing branch. Unknotting number minimizes crossing-change counts over regular diagrams of representatives, including zero changes.

The descending procedure receives an admissible one-component finite planar code and an edge-interior basepoint; it switches precisely the crossings first encountered underneath. Crossing-free input returns an empty list.
The geometric bridge and descending-diagram results assume countable choice; the Seifert-matrix crossing-change and signature results assume full AC.
Hermitian signature counts positive eigenvalues minus negative eigenvalues, with multiplicity and with zero eigenvalues omitted.

Bridge-sphere normalization fixes the knot and bridge sphere, permits punctures to travel along the knot, and assumes both π₁-injectivity and absence of boundary compressions for the decomposing annulus.

load_bearing.statement: Under countable choice and the stated essential-annulus hypotheses, the specified decomposing sphere can be isotoped, changing only the spanning-disk systems for the fixed bridge pair, so that its intersection with the bridge sphere is one circle and its intersection with the spanning disks consists of exactly two puncture-to-circle arcs.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every finite rational polygonal code that records one oriented circle, finitely many transverse double points, and one overpassing branch at each double point, and every basepoint in the interior of an edge, if the first encounter at each crossing is the overpassing branch, then the represented knot is ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the standard unknot.

Under countable choice, a smooth proper arc in an upper height ball with exactly one nondegenerate interior maximum and no other critical point bounds an embedded disk with every prescribed simple smooth joining arc on the boundary level sphere; the corresponding lower-ball minimum assertion also holds.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let D₊ and D₋ be finite regular oriented diagrams that agree outside one crossing neighborhood and differ inside it by switching which branch is over. Let V₊ and V₋ be the Seifert matrices obtained from their oriented disk-and-band surfaces. There are corresponding integral bases in which either V₊=V₋ or V₊−V₋=±vvᵀ for some integral column vector v. In particular, rank(V₊−V₋)≤1.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every smooth oriented knot in S³ has an admissible finite planar code whose rational polygonal drawing certificate represents a regular oriented diagram of that knot.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice used by the bridge-number definition. For every smooth oriented knot K in the standard S³, b(K)=1 if and only if K is ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the fixed oriented coordinate circle used as the standard unknot.

Let A and B be Hermitian forms on the same finite-dimensional complex vector space, and suppose that the linear map representing A−B has rank at most one. Then |sign(A)−sign(B)|≤2, where the signature is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues, with multiplicity and with zero eigenvalues omitted.

seams_checked.note: Checked the finite one-component code interface, positive-meridian source/target conjugacy, constructor and correctness statements against their uses. The trefoil relations use the supplier's stated conjugacy direction.

The linking interface is consumed through the positive-push Seifert-pairing definition. Its positive-meridian normalization and full-AC hypothesis agree with the opened signed-intersection supplier; no opposite sign convention is introduced.

Connected-sum datum independence, sphere capping, genus-zero characterization, compatible Schoenflies ball parameters and the unknot identity are used with their smooth oriented domains and countable-choice hypotheses retained.

The consumer uses only the classical value at −1. It proves nonsingularity there using the unimodular skew part before invoking the nonroot signature interface, so it does not confuse actual matrix signature with the supplier's root-average convention.

Schubert's proof uses the opened meridian-homology lemma solely for H₁(E; Z)=Z[μ], with a chosen product tube. Sending the annulus generator to ±1 establishes the required π₁ injection without importing any trace or sliceness claim.
